title: Tesla's flying Roadster
ticker: Tesla's new Roadster drives upside down, flies and lands in Texas demo
Musk: "Turns out the future does have flying cars"
Tesla claims 0-60 mph in 0.81 seconds - not yet independently verified
Production not expected before 2028 - price not announced

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Welcome to KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Tesla has finally shown off its long-awaited new *Roadster*, and it did things you would never expect from a car.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: It drove *upside down* on a giant curved ramp, launched into the air, *flipped*, and landed back on its wheels.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Elon Musk says it proves the future has *flying cars*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We look at what Tesla showed, how it works, and the big questions it left *unanswered*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The reveal was livestreamed, with Musk on stage alongside Tesla design chief *Franz von Holzhausen* and engineering vice president *Lars Moravy*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Musk promised *some crazy stuff*, and compared the car to *James Bond's* gadget-loaded car.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He warned that success was *not guaranteed*. But, he said, *excitement is 100 percent guaranteed*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The demonstration took place on Thursday night at a *SpaceX facility* in McGregor, Texas.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Reporters from *Reuters* were there to witness it.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The redesigned Roadster sped up a massive *curved ramp*, and kept driving as the ramp curled over, until the car was *upside down*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Then it *launched into the air*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: As it rotated, powerful bursts of *compressed air* helped control its movement, before it landed safely back on its wheels.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: One outlet said it looked more like a *Hollywood stunt show* than a traditional car launch.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: *Well, it worked*, Musk joked after the stunt, as the audience cheered.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: *Flying cars are real*, added Lars Moravy, Tesla's vice president of vehicle engineering.

scenes.name: Elon Musk
scenes.post: Turns out the future does have flying cars

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Musk later posted the video on X with a short caption. *Turns out the future does have flying cars.*

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Tesla's official account shared it too, writing simply: *Real life, baby.*

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: One clip of the stunt racked up about *1.7 million views*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The footage spread fast on X, drawing reactions from public figures including Florida Governor *Ron DeSantis* and Congresswoman *Elise Stefanik*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: So how does a car stick to a ramp *upside down*, and then fly?

items.text: Suction keeps the car stuck to the surface
Bursts of compressed air steer it midair

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The trick is two systems working together.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: First, a *fan-powered system* creates enough suction to keep the car pressed against a surface, even when it is *upside down*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Tesla calls it a *multi-mode suction system*. It works like a so-called *fan car*, a design that has been used on race cars before.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Second, *cold-gas thrusters* developed with SpaceX, Musk's rocket company.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: They release bursts of *high-pressure gas* to create thrust. On spacecraft, the same kind of thruster is used to steer in orbit.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: That is what lets the Roadster *lift off* the ground and adjust its position in midair.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Tesla also showed a recorded *acceleration test*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In it, the Roadster went from zero to 60 miles an hour in just *0.81 seconds*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: That would make it one of the *fastest-accelerating* vehicles ever built.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: But that number has *not been independently verified*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Not everyone is convinced Tesla is still *ahead of the pack*.

items.text: Fan car that drives upside down
Yangwang U9 hypercar that can jump

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Electric car site *Electrek* pointed out that Tesla is no longer the first to many of these tricks.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Britain's *McMurtry Spierling*, a fan car, has already driven upside down.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: China's *BYD* has shown its Yangwang U9 hypercar *jumping* over potholes, using active suspension.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Meanwhile, electric cars from Croatia's *Rimac* and China's *Xiaomi* have been setting speed and lap records.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Electrek also questioned some numbers on Tesla's display, saying the claimed *4,700 kilograms* of downforce seems potentially *unreal* for a small two-seater.

scenes.name: Wall Street
scenes.quote: Tesla shares closed at $362.44 on Thursday, down 1.29%, before the evening reveal. Q3 earnings: October 21.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Wall Street, Tesla shares closed down *1.3 percent* on Thursday, before the reveal.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Analysts say the Roadster could give the stock a *short-lived* boost, but investors are focused on Tesla's *earnings report* on October twenty-first.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Earlier this month, Tesla reported about *486,000* deliveries for the quarter, beating forecasts, but still *down* from a year earlier.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Musk himself has said the Roadster will *not move* Tesla's finances in a major way.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: For many Tesla fans, the bigger surprise is that the Roadster *showed up at all*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Tesla's very first car, back in 2008, was also called the *Roadster*. The new one was meant to be its triumphant return.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Tesla first unveiled the second-generation Roadster back in *November 2017*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It promised zero to 60 in *1.9 seconds*, a top speed over 250 miles an hour, and a range of up to *620 miles*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Deliveries were supposed to start in *2020*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Customers paid a *50,000 dollar* deposit to reserve one. A limited Founders Series cost *250,000 dollars* up front.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: But production was delayed again and again, as Tesla focused on mass-market cars, the Cybertruck, and self-driving. Some buyers *asked for refunds*.

scenes.name: Elon Musk
scenes.role: CEO, Tesla · earlier post on X
scenes.quote: This will actually be able to fly very briefly. I always laughed at flying cars & now making one.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Musk has teased a flying Roadster for years.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He once said an optional *SpaceX package* would let the car fly *very briefly*, in short hops.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: I always laughed at flying cars, he wrote, and *now making one*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He warned the ride would be safe, but *very intense*, like a hardcore roller coaster.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Back in 2019, he gave more detail: the thrusters would use *ultra-high pressure air*, stored in a tank *in place of the two rear seats*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He promised a mind-blowing demo more than once. Last November, on Joe Rogan's podcast, he teased an *unforgettable* one.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: The demo was spectacular. But can anyone actually *buy one*, and *drive it*?

items.text: No approval to fly on public roads
How long it can stay airborne

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Tesla did not announce a *final price*, or detailed production specs.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The original base model was listed at *200,000 dollars*. Delays and the SpaceX package could push that higher.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The demo was done under *controlled conditions*, and there is no sign the car has any approval to fly on *public roads*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Under U.S. rules, vehicles that leave the ground are usually treated as *aircraft*, overseen by the *FAA*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Asked whether the Roadster is street legal, Musk joked: *Depends on your street.*

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Musk himself has called the Roadster an *engineering showcase*, not a big money-maker, and maybe one of Tesla's last cars designed mainly for *human drivers*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Production is not expected before *2028*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Tesla proved it can get a Roadster *into the air* and back down safely.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Turning that into a car people can *buy and drive* is the next challenge.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We'll be watching Tesla's *earnings call* on October twenty-first for any update on the Roadster.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: If you found this helpful, please *like and subscribe* for more.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: This has been KOWEN News. Thanks for watching.
